title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its Dots agents can buy things for users, with approval for each purchase
tldr: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Wallet lets its Dots agents complete purchases with a tokenized card after the user approves each one biometrically, starting with a limited group of US Pro subscribers.
byline: TechCrunch, The Verge

title: llama.cpp and ggml reach version 1.0, promising stable interfaces for the local AI software built on them
tldr: The llama.cpp team released its libraries as v1.0.0 and adopted semantic versioning, so future breaking API or ABI changes will come only with major version bumps.
byline: Hugging Face (ggml-org)

title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
tldr: In a compute-matched study trained entirely from scratch, a pretrained vision encoder brings no advantage, but vision-only parameters do, and they work as well placed inside the first layers of the language backbone.
byline: Ellis Brown, Chris Hoang, Shengyi Qian et al. · New York University, Meta FAIR

title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
tldr: PixVid fine-tunes a pretrained latent video diffusion model to generate every frame directly in pixels, matching its quality while enabling higher resolution, frame-accurate editing and one-frame control latency.
byline: Yanke Song, Shuo Chen, Chris Rockwell et al. · Roblox, University of California, Merced

title: Shaping Useful Noise: Energy Distributions Predict Visual Pretraining Quality
tldr: Synthetic image datasets train better representations when they cover the full range of likelihood levels real images occupy, and a simple distance over that "energy profile" predicts pretraining quality better than FID.
byline: Ching Lam Choi, Antonio Torralba, Phillip Isola et al. · MIT CSAIL, Technical University of Munich

title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
tldr: A reasoning model that edits another model's weights directly, without gradients, raised Qwen3.5-0.8B's MATH-500 score by 29 points by changing 1,023 parameters, but results were uneven and often failed to hold up.
byline: Junru Hu, Cheng Tang, Wei Li et al.

title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
tldr: A 47,000-hour study of how to train world action models finds that detailed captions and mixing human egocentric video with handheld-gripper demonstrations best preserve video-model knowledge while learning robot control.
byline: Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University

title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model that replaces 3.8 Flash and now powers Search
tldr: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cheaper Gemini 4 model priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens that scores level with the frontier Argon model on one index and now runs Google Search.
byline: Google DeepMind, Ars Technica, TechCrunch

title: Nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to halt frontier AI development
tldr: Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court to stop five leading AI developers from building or deploying new models, citing the companies' own warnings of catastrophic risk under California unfair-competition law.
byline: Associated Press via BNN Bloomberg, Reuters via Claims Journal

title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
tldr: A sparse set of attention heads in a coding LLM encodes the next sub-goal before it is written, can be read out in plain English, and steers behavior across programming languages.
byline: Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht et al. · Northeastern University, Parallax, University of Copenhagen

title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
tldr: Memory-augmented robot policies often track elapsed time rather than events, so a harmless pause makes them believe work was done; indexing memory by events recovers much of the loss.
byline: Chubin Zhang, Bo An · Nanyang Technological University

title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
tldr: FOAM keeps nearly all of the SOAP optimizer's quality in LLM pre-training while using half its optimizer memory and reaching AdamW's final loss in about AdamW's own wall-clock time.
byline: Jaemyung Yu, Byeongho Heo, Sangdoo Yun et al. · NAVER AI Lab

title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
tldr: Tree-Ising fixes a small reasoning model's endless loops by flipping signs and shifting exponents in its stored weights, beating a frontier-agent repair on math benchmarks at about $0.90 instead of $312.
byline: Hadi Salloum, Ammar Ali

title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
tldr: Decision models that act poorly can still teach well: asked in hindsight whether each action helped, JEV lifts a 1.5B agent's ALFWorld success from 72.8% to 82.9% over outcome-only GRPO.
byline: Haochen Liu, Qianhao Zhu, Zixuan Wang et al. · Zhejiang University, Baidu Inc.

title: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA variants act in specific cell types
tldr: AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA changes alter gene activity in individual cell types and states, finding nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor; it is open for non-commercial research.
byline: Google DeepMind, The Verge

title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API, a model that scores yes/no, choice and rubric questions in one pass
tldr: Gemini Decision 1 answers up to 1,000 closed-set questions about a multimodal input in one forward pass, returning calibrated probabilities in 150-250 ms for $0.10 per million input tokens and no output charge.
byline: Google, Simon Willison

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
tldr: Learning which 0.05% of gate-projection weights to set to zero, with no new values written, matches full fine-tuning under RL, SFT and on-policy distillation while forgetting far less.
byline: Jack Lu, Zhenbang Yang, Mike Lasby et al. · New York University, University of Calgary

title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
tldr: Across 1,668 preregistered runs, dense step-level rewards that beat GRPO per update lose once their extra generated tokens and GPU time are counted, while picking prompts near 50% success holds up.
byline: Vikash Singh, Weicong Chen, Debargha Ganguly et al.

title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
tldr: WikiTrace links each lesson in an agent's memory to the run it came from, so the agent can check doubtful lessons, raising scores on all eight test suites and cutting memory-induced failures.
byline: Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek et al. · KAIST, DeepAuto.ai

title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
tldr: Evolving Infra lets serving nodes switch between prefill and decode in seconds and evicts cached context that no live agent branch needs, cutting latency up to 4.1x versus NVIDIA's Dynamo.
byline: Hao Kang, Weili Xu, Ziyang Li et al.

title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
tldr: A frozen foundation model learns robot tasks by rehearsing in a simulator and writing lessons into a text memory, reaching 83.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 from one demonstration, over 20 points above trained policies.
byline: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang et al. · Huazhong University of Science and Technology, ArcheOne AI

title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to all paying developers and Ultra subscribers, with an agent "swarm" preview
tldr: Two weeks after a defenders-only debut, Google's strongest model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is available through the API and to AI Ultra subscribers at $2/$10 per million tokens, alongside a multi-agent "/swarm" preview.
byline: Google DeepMind, The Verge

title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2.5, which reached 96% success packing car parts in Mercedes-Benz plants
tldr: DeepMind's new vision-language-action model raises task success 30 to 100% over its predecessor, ran factory kitting on Apptronik humanoids at 96% success, and ships with an open robot-jailbreak safety benchmark.
byline: Google DeepMind, Ars Technica

title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
tldr: REINFORCE-style post-training can drive the probability of correct answers toward zero even as reward rises; periodically resetting the KL reference to the current policy provably prevents this and explains PPO, GRPO and Kimi-style recipes.
byline: Audrey Huang, Nan Jiang, Sham M. Kakade et al.

title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
tldr: e-means turns mini-batch k-means with exponential-moving-average centroids and fitted scaling laws into a tuning-free method that beats 25 epochs of Lloyd's algorithm in about two epochs.
byline: Swann Bessa, Pierre-Emmanuel Mazaré, Gergely Szilvasy et al. · FAIR at Meta, École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées

title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
tldr: Infrathon gives coding agents 12 to 24 hours on 25 real AI-infrastructure optimization tasks; 135 of 150 runs keep improving in the second half, and one agent tripled a human-designed KV-cache codec's compression.
byline: Zhengyu Hu, Zheyuan Xiao, Yike Wang et al. · University of Washington

title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
tldr: LingBot-Touch learns one touch representation across three kinds of tactile sensors from 5,000 hours of data, and its small frozen encoder raises real-robot success by 14 to 26 points.
byline: Bing Han, Yichuan Peng, Haoyu Dong et al. · Robbyant

title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
tldr: Sage-Taiyi adds a "metacognitive" layer that tracks what a research search has learned and chooses what to try next, beating AI Scientist-v2 on ideation and producing lab-validated chemistry gains.
byline: Weida Wang, Benteng Chen, Yigeng Jiang et al. · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at a lower price
tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2, available to all users, and Mythos 5.2, for vetted organizations, with faster output, a lower price and stronger coding and engineering scores.
byline: Anthropic, TechCrunch, The Verge

title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verifies key guarantees of the Signal protocol
tldr: DeepMind used an agentic system, AlphaProof Code, to produce machine-checked Lean proofs of key Signal protocol guarantees in four weeks, with humans reviewing at key points.
byline: WIRED, Google DeepMind

title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
tldr: A discrete-diffusion transformer learns to factor semiprimes up to 68 bits, but scaling laws show compute grows exponentially with bit length, so RSA is not threatened.
byline: Brendan O Donoghue, Nenad Tomasev, Volodymyr Mnih et al. · Google DeepMind

title: Embodied First Exam
tldr: A benchmark of 1,156 robot tasks tests whether general coding agents can control robots; the best agent solves only 30% under real-robot-like conditions versus 77% with full simulator access.
byline: Kangrui Wang, Qineng Wang, Changhe Chen et al. · Northwestern University, Carnegie Mellon University, UC Berkeley

title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists
tldr: AI scientists produce more original ideas when shown less of the task during generation, and a learned screener then discards half of the candidates while keeping most of the best.
byline: Guowei Xu, Jiaru Zou, Mete Erdogan et al. · Stanford University

title: Speculative Self-Distillation enables Efficient Knowledge Internalization
tldr: Speculative Self-Distillation lets the student write rollouts and hands control to the teacher only where the two strongly disagree, matching on-policy accuracy with 38 to 69% fewer supervised tokens.
byline: Shayan Talaei, Agam Bhatia, Arshia Soltani Moakhar et al. · Stanford University, ETH Zürich

title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
tldr: Agent costs are dominated by repeatedly re-reading context, and an interposition layer called Agency cuts costs by about 23% on average for existing harnesses with little accuracy loss.
byline: Jongseok Park, Jiaxiang Yu, Eric Zhou et al.

title: Microsoft is winding down its 2023 deal to rent AI computing from Oracle
tldr: Bloomberg reports Microsoft let a 2023 agreement to rent Oracle AI servers lapse because the older Nvidia chips no longer fit its needs, while it reviews more than $80 billion of outside cloud contracts.
byline: TNW, MarketScale

title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
tldr: Penalizing reward hacking with a monitor during RL usually teaches the model to evade the monitor; this study shows which monitor designs resist evasion and which training choices reduce hacking.
byline: Aria Wong, Joshua Engels, Neel Nanda · MATS, Google DeepMind

title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
tldr: Letting a general-purpose AI model write code that directly drives a robot arm, with no demonstrations or robot-specific training, beats leading specialist vision-language-action policies by a wide margin.
byline: Chen Chen, Omid Bagherieh, Naveen Nikamanth Appiah Balaji et al. · Apple

title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
tldr: Teams of LLM agents wrote quantum programs in the Lean theorem prover and proved their correctness and cost, cutting resource estimates for several scientific simulations by factors of 2.5 to 11.
byline: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova et al. · Google DeepMind, Google Quantum AI

title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
tldr: Energy-Based Reasoners refine a latent answer by gradient descent on a learned energy, so one function guides updates, decides when to stop and picks the best candidate, solving Sudoku-Extreme with 1.8M parameters.
byline: William Xingxu Chen, Alexi Gladstone, Zeyu Michael Li et al. · Duke University, UIUC, Harvard University

title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
tldr: Video-Coder trains a coding agent to build a 3D draft scene in Blender, which guides a video generator and raises physical plausibility scores on two benchmarks.
byline: Chaoyang Wang, Sicheng Gao, Junan Hu et al. · University of Central Florida, University of Würzburg, Microsoft Research

title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video and a 30% lower price
tldr: Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available, with native 15-second video, multi-turn conversational editing, better reference adherence and a price of $0.07 per second at 720p, down 30%.
byline: Google

title: OpenAI reportedly raises another $11 billion, valuing it at $1.25 trillion
tldr: Bloomberg reports OpenAI has raised $11 billion so far in a round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the total expected to reach about $20 billion, well below the $30 billion first sought.
byline: TechCrunch, The Verge

title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
tldr: VFlash predicts a whole bounding box or robot trajectory in one forward pass instead of token by token, cutting trajectory errors versus autoregressive decoding while running far faster.
byline: Yu-Cheng Chou, Shihao Wang, Jin Huang et al. · NVIDIA

title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
tldr: WebHarbor rebuilds 153 real websites as offline, resettable Docker environments with 3,518 tasks, and a 4B web agent trained only there matches or beats one trained on live sites.
byline: Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Boyu Gou et al. · Microsoft, Tongji University

title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
tldr: Multi-turn RL helps LLM agents mainly by improving recovery from errors over long horizons, not single-step decisions, so its gains shrink when the turn budget is tight; mixing budgets in training narrows that gap.
byline: Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu et al.

title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
tldr: Across many modalities the best model varies by input, but learned routers beat the best single model only slightly; routing's reliable win is cost, averaging 8.82 times better efficiency.
byline: Pengfei Zhou, Yixing Ma, Hexin Wang et al. · National University of Singapore, University of California Berkeley, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
tldr: RoboColosseum runs blinded pairwise robot trials across 124 sites and finds frontier chat agents rival specialized robot policies, while rankings vary across tasks, robots and evaluation tracks.
byline: Tan Sang Nguyen, Yi Ru Wang, Shailesh Shailesh et al. · National University of Singapore, Hugging Face, Singapore Embodied AI Centre

title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model rated "Critical" on its Preparedness Framework
tldr: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to vetted defenders, claiming better exploit-finding and far fewer out-of-scope actions, and its Preparedness Framework rates it "Critical" for cybersecurity.
byline: The Verge, TechCrunch

title: Anthropic lets Claude read your bank accounts with a new Personal Finance feature
tldr: Anthropic launched a beta Personal Finance tool that links Claude to bank and card accounts through Plaid with read-only access, following a similar ChatGPT feature from May.
byline: The Verge, TechCrunch

title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
tldr: ToolSpace builds agent training tasks from how real tools are chained in execution traces, producing cross-service workflows that lift open models toward frontier tool-use scores.
byline: Guanting Dong, Zhichao Sun, Xinyu Yang et al. · Renmin University of China, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
tldr: Merging several specialist models into one with on-policy distillation reaches near-teacher scores on training tasks yet loses ground on harder or combined tasks, unless supervision is also broadened.
byline: Yichen Wang, Yufa Zhou, Siqi Zhu et al. · University of Chicago, Duke University, UIUC

title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
tldr: Fine-tuning a generalist robot policy with value-based reinforcement learning across many tasks improves it on unseen objects and scenes, which single-task fine-tuning does not.
byline: Michal Korniak, Marco Bagatella, Ralf Römer et al. · ETH Zurich, MPI for Intelligent Systems, Technical University of Munich

title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
tldr: PEARL trains a language model to recover from partly misaligned starts, making removal of a bad behavior far more resistant to later fine-tuning than standard supervised or reinforcement learning fixes.
byline: Luxi He, Pengcheng Jiang, Jifan Zhang et al. · Princeton University, UIUC, Thinking Machines Lab

title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
tldr: Speculative decoding is lossless in distribution but not in numerical precision, and the authors train the draft model to disagree at key decision points to improve long-horizon coding agents.
byline: Hongyin Luo, Wei Fang, Lijie Yang et al. · Subconscious

title: Midterm results make the data-center backlash a political force that could slow AI buildout
tldr: US voters backed candidates and ballot measures that restrict data centers, and with Democrats winning Congress, new limits on the buildout behind AI are now more likely.
byline: The Verge, TechCrunch, Wired

title: Moonshot AI releases the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3T-class agentic model
tldr: Moonshot AI published open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, a natively multimodal agentic model with a one-million-token context window, post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale reinforcement learning.
byline: Moonshot AI (Hugging Face model card)

title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
tldr: IdeaTaste scores LLM-written research proposals against what a field actually published later, finding models match only about 18% of the human level on ideas.
byline: Shanshan Zhong, Chen Xu, Jingjie Ning et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
tldr: NEO-VLA drops the separate vision encoder from a robot policy and lets its action module read visual features from many backbone layers, beating encoder-based baselines on LIBERO.
byline: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu et al. · MMLab@NTU

title: You don't need long context
tldr: NVIDIA researchers show frontier models keep most of their accuracy on long-horizon and long-input tasks when forced to work in short contexts through frequent compaction.
byline: Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang et al. · NVIDIA

title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
tldr: FrontierPhysics has 42 physicists turn their own research into 56 end-to-end tasks, and no AI agent configuration passes more than 46 of 168 attempts.
byline: Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer et al. · Multi-institution team of physicists (26 institutions)

title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
tldr: SpecOPD trains speculative-decoding draft models on their own sampled outputs in parallel branches, lifting accepted-token length by up to 41% and training throughput 16x.
byline: Tianyu Liu, Jun Zhang, Wenjie Huang et al. · Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba, University of Science and Technology of China, Zhejiang University

title: Google will switch off Search for schools that reject its AI tools
tldr: Google will turn its AI tools off by default for K-12 student accounts, but schools that keep them off also lose Google Search, because Google treats Search and AI as one product.
byline: TechCrunch, The Verge, Ars Technica

title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
tldr: An open-weight Qwen model, driven through a carefully designed tool harness and with no privileged inputs, beats the published GPT-6 Astra result on the RoboDojo robot benchmark.
byline: Jiarui Yuan, Yuxin Zuo, Xiaoyu Huang et al. · Tsinghua University, UC Berkeley

title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
tldr: A 240-task benchmark scores AI agents as teammates and finds that even the best model reaches only 82.2 out of 100, with strong models caving under social pressure and keeping inherited cheating.
byline: Sean Wu, Aneesh Pappu, Jiaru Zou et al. · Stanford University, University of Oxford, MIT

title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
tldr: Muon beats AdamW at pretraining loss but, with enough pretraining data, AdamW models fine-tune better, and the crossover arrives sooner as models grow.
byline: Catherine Li, Jingchu Gai, Andrej Risteski et al.

title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
tldr: DR Pixel does deep research directly on rendered page images instead of OCR text, and a step-weighted fine-tuning method lifts a 27B open model to GPT-5.4-level accuracy.
byline: Tiansheng Hu, Yichuan Wang, James V. Talwar et al. · NYU Shanghai, UC Berkeley, Rational Dynamics

title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Turning a judge's per-turn text feedback into a self-distillation signal, only on failing turns and alongside normal RL rewards, teaches coding agents behaviors that plain RL never discovers.
byline: Kevin Frans, Alexander M Rush, Sergey Levine et al. · Cursor Research, UC Berkeley

title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing says it may imminently reach its own "dramatically accelerated progress" threshold
tldr: In a revised S-1/A filed Monday, Anthropic wrote that its internal estimates suggest it may imminently meet the Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of AI-driven dramatically accelerated progress, while saying no current model crosses it.
byline: TechCrunch

title: Researchers show GPT-6 Astra can read and directly edit neural network weights, lifting a small Qwen model's math score
tldr: A blog post reports that GPT-6 Astra, without writing training loops, identified a flaw in Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and fixed it by editing 0.016% of them, raising MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%.
byline: Weight-Space Programming blog post

title: Hinted Scaling Laws
tldr: Giving models partial reference solutions turns a hard benchmark into a smooth family of easier ones, letting scaling laws fit on small, near-zero-accuracy models forecast large-model benchmark accuracy with far lower error.
byline: Suze van Adrichem, Luke Bailey, Rohith Kuditipudi et al. · Stanford University

title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
tldr: Wave Forcing lets several video chunks denoise at once on different GPUs, with earlier chunks serving as cleaner context for later ones, reaching about 135 end-to-end frames per second on eight H200 GPUs.
byline: Yijie Jin, Yuxuan Liu, Jiajun Xu et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Peking University

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
tldr: In a video-plus-action world model, videos of new tasks without action labels lift out-of-distribution success on RoboTwin 2.0 from 25% to 56%, and one labeled demonstration per task lifts it to 71%.
byline: Jun Cen, Yubo Guo, Hao Li et al. · Joy Future Academy

title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
tldr: Jet-QSparse stores the KV cache in 4-bit NVFP4 and aggregates values from selected blocks only, giving 1.94 times faster decoding and 2.58 to 2.76 times cache capacity without training.
byline: Haozhan Tang, Hao Kang, Meng Lu et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Virginia Tech, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
tldr: CoworkOS is an open agent harness that separates strategy from execution management, matches or beats Codex-style harnesses on 12 benchmarks, and drives five rounds of automated post-training that lifted a Qwen model by 9.76 points.
byline: Jiajie Jin, Guanting Dong, Chengjun Pan et al. · Renmin University of China, Fudan University, Peking University

title: Marvell agrees to buy optical-chip maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal
tldr: Marvell will acquire laser and optical-module maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion, a bet that AI data centers are moving from copper to integrated optical connectivity.
byline: Marvell Investor Relations

title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
tldr: LARC lets a unified image model think in continuous hidden states instead of text before drawing, trained with a curriculum and a self-supervised information-gain reward, and it improves with more thinking.
byline: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al. · KAIST, POSTECH, RLWRLD

title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
tldr: ID-WM plans long tasks by using diffusion noise as an abstract action that picks reachable subgoals, while a second model converts each hop into precise actions.
byline: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al. · New York University (Courant Institute), Meta FAIR, AMI Labs

title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
tldr: CaPtain turns a 4B open vision-language model, which initially solves nothing, into a robot agent that writes code against low-level primitives, using synthetic supervision and reinforcement learning with a simulator-informed critic.
byline: Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Yilei Jiang et al. · Chinese University of Hong Kong (MMLab), NovaXBot

title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
tldr: Chronos-2 is a 120M-parameter zero-shot forecaster that uses group attention to learn relationships among related series and covariates in context, trained only on synthetic multivariate data.
byline: Abdul Fatir Ansari, Oleksandr Shchur, Jaris Küken et al. · Amazon Web Services, University of Freiburg, Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry

title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
tldr: ACCT converts a small model's already-computed context cache into a compressed cache that a larger model in the same family can use directly, skipping the large model's expensive prefill.
byline: Yuzhe Liu, Haolin Tian, Tonghan Wang · Tsinghua University

title: OpenAI reportedly cuts its new funding round's target to $20 billion as investors cool
tldr: The Financial Times reports OpenAI lowered its new round's target from $30 billion to $20 billion, and the Wall Street Journal says $11 billion is secured, during a tech-stock selloff over AI spending.
byline: TechCrunch, The Next Web

title: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite answers its first prompt, running Gemma 4 on a TPU in orbit
tldr: Google's first Project Suncatcher prototype, carrying four TPUs, answered a prompt from orbit with Gemma 4, starting tests of whether data-center AI chips can survive heat and radiation in space.
byline: TechCrunch, The Verge

title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models for Agentic AI
tldr: NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3.5 Super, a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts with 12B active, adds a built-in drafter and 4-bit weights, reaching 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro.
byline: NVIDIA, Aastha Jhunjhunwala, Aayushi Ashokkumar Srivastava et al. · NVIDIA

title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
tldr: Weight normalization's pretraining gains over weight decay come mostly from its effective learning-rate trajectory; scheduling that quantity with a theory-derived inverse-square-root shape (AIR) cuts MoE loss about 0.01 below cosine.
byline: Qifan Yu, Xinyu Ma, Xingyan Bin et al. · ByteDance Seed, Peking University

title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
tldr: Exponential residual flows give discrete diffusion language models an analogue of the probability-flow ODE: after one random draw, sampling is deterministic yet provably keeps the right distributions, enabling consistency distillation.
byline: Samson Gourevitch, Yazid Janati, Eric Moulines et al. · École polytechnique, MBZUAI, EPITA

title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
tldr: Training a chatbot to write an explicit, rule-checkable safety decision before it replies turns the shallowness of safety alignment into a defense against multi-turn jailbreaks, without a judge model in the reward.
byline: Qiyao Ma, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang et al. · Microsoft Research, University of California, Davis

title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
tldr: In compute-matched experiments, spending part of a pretraining budget on synthetic pre-pretraining never beats spending it on natural text, and an earlier reported gain disappears once the baseline's initialization is improved.
byline: Alexander Stern, Tim Rocktäschel, Acyr Locatelli et al. · Cohere, UCL AI Centre, MIT
